title: Bounded double graph open in a projective Hilbert scheme
statement: Let $U$ be a Noetherian affine scheme, meaning affine and locally Noetherian [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $X\to U$ and $Y\to U$ be proper, flat and finitely presented morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose that $E=X\times_UY$ has a specified closed immersion $j:E\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_U$ for some $m\ge0$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-kun-projective]. Let $R\in\mathbf Q[n]$ be a numerical polynomial (integer-valued on integers). Assume that for every geometric point $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, and every isomorphism $f:X_t\simeq Y_t$, the closed graph of $f$ has coordinate Hilbert polynomial $R$ for $j_t$ [def-sfb-projective-coordinate-hilbert-polynomial]. Let $\operatorname{Hilb}_{E/U}$ assign to a $U$-scheme $T$ the closed subschemes $D\subset E_T$ flat and finitely presented over $T$, with pullback as transition maps; since $E$ is projective, these are proper [def-sfb-proper-hilbert-presheaf]. This functor has a representative $H=\coprod_P H_P$ with $H_P$ representing the families whose geometric fibres have polynomial $P$, each $H_P$ projective over $U$. There are open subschemes $H_X,H_Y\subset H$ [def-weil-open-immersion] characterized, on every $U$-scheme $T$, by invertibility respectively of the projections $D\to X_T$ and $D\to Y_T$ of the corresponding universal closed family. Their intersection $J=H_X\cap H_Y$ factors through $H_R$ as an open subscheme, is Noetherian and quasi-compact, and $J\to U$ is separated and of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated). For every $T\to U$, its points are naturally exactly the closed subschemes $D\subset X_T\times_TY_T$ with both projections $p_X,p_Y$ invertible; such a $D$ is the graph of the isomorphism $p_Y\circ p_X^{-1}$ and every isomorphism has exactly this graph. The representative, its universal graph, the two projection identities, and these inverse bijections commute with every base change of test schemes, including nonreduced ones, and with arbitrary $U'\to U$ by pulling back $J$ and $H_R$; $U'$ need not be Noetherian. No bound on fibre dimension is assumed beyond the stated fixed-polynomial hypothesis.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability] to the given embedding over the Noetherian scheme $U$. It gives $H=\coprod_P H_P$, each $H_P$ projective, its stated fibre-polynomial subfunctor, and the universal closed family with arbitrary base change. These are also the proper Hilbert families: $E\to X$ is a base change of the proper map $Y\to U$, so $E\to U$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. For every $T\to U$, $E_T\to T$ remains proper; every closed $D\subset E_T$ is proper over $T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Thus the Hilbert functor here equals the proper Hilbert functor to which the graph theorem applies.

source.place: Tags 0CZY (situation-hilb), 0D1A (lemma-Mor-into-Hilb); projective representative supplied by the cited Hilbert node; proper permanence Tags 01W4, 01W3, 01W5

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-graphs-open-in-hilbert] with $(Z,X)=(X,Y)$: $X\to U$ is proper, flat and finitely presented, and $Y\to U$ is separated because it is proper. On the universal family this gives $H_X\subset H$, characterized for every $T\to H$ by invertibility of $p_X:D\to X_T$. Apply the same theorem with $(Z,X)=(Y,X)$, identifying $Y\times_U X$ with $E$ by swapping the projections. It gives $H_Y\subset H$, characterized by invertibility of $p_Y$. Both are open subschemes; restricting the structure sheaf of $H$ to their set-theoretic intersection defines the open subscheme $J=H_X\cap H_Y$. Its $T$-points impose both conditions on the same closed family.

source.place: Tags 0D1A and 0D1B (lemma-Mor-into-Hilb and lemma-Mor-into-Hilb-open), applied twice

proof.text: For $D$ classified by a $T$-point of $J$, set $f=p_Y\circ p_X^{-1}$; it is an isomorphism, with inverse $p_X\circ p_Y^{-1}$. If $i:D\hookrightarrow X_T\times_TY_T$ is its inclusion, then $i\circ p_X^{-1}$ has components $\mathrm{id}_{X_T}$ and $f$, so it equals $(\mathrm{id},f)$ by the fibre-product mapping property. Hence $D$ is exactly the graph of $f$ as a closed subscheme. Conversely [lem-sfb-graphs-open-in-hilbert] assigns every isomorphism $f$ its graph, on which the projections are $\mathrm{id}$ and $f$ and therefore invertible. These operations are inverse: recovering $f$ gives $f$, and recovering $D$ gives the same closed immersion via $p_X$. This also proves uniqueness of the graph.

source.place: Tag 0D1A (lemma-Mor-into-Hilb), final proof paragraph, and Tag 0D1B, graph criterion

proof.text: For any point $a\in J$ choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of its residue field and the geometric point $\bar a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to J$. Step 3 identifies its universal family with an isomorphism graph over the geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$. By the fixed-polynomial hypothesis its polynomial is $R$. The stratum characterization in [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability] therefore puts $a$ in $H_R$. Consequently the inverse image in $J$ of the open complement $\coprod_{P\ne R}H_P$ is empty. Restricting the map $J\to H$ to the open $H_R$ gives a unique factorization, and $J\to H_R$ is the inclusion of the same open subset with its restricted structure sheaf. This uses factorization through an open, so it holds with the full scheme structures, including nilpotents.

source.place: Tag 0DSQ (lemma-curves-diagonal-separated-fp), final bounded-open argument, with the fixed coordinate-polynomial assumption replacing the preceding curve calculation

proof.text: The morphism $H_R\to U$ is of finite type by [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability]. Since $U$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $H_R$ Noetherian. Its open subscheme $J$ is Noetherian, hence quasi-compact, by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Both $J$ and $U$ are locally Noetherian, hence quasi-separated schemes by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) to $J\to U$: its source is quasi-compact and target quasi-separated, so this map is quasi-compact; its source is quasi-separated, so the map is quasi-separated.

The diagonal of $J\to U$ is the pullback of the diagonal of $H_R\to U$ along $J\times_UJ\to H_R\times_UH_R$: a pair of maps to $J$ has equal images in $H_R$ precisely when the maps are equal, since an open inclusion is injective on maps, with the same restricted sheaf. The Hilbert node says $H_R\to U$ is separated, so its diagonal is a closed immersion. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] the displayed pullback is a closed immersion. This proves that $J\to U$ is separated.

source.place: Tag 01KK (definition-separated), diagonal restricted to an open source; Tag 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion), closed case

proof.text: To verify local finite presentation without any finiteness assumption on test schemes, take an affine base open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ from a Noetherian-ring affine cover of $U$. The finite-type assertion for $H_R\to U$ in [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability] gives an affine cover over $V$ by $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a finite-type $A$-algebra. For each point of $J\cap W$ choose a distinguished open $D(s)\subseteq J\cap W$ containing it. If $B=A[b_1,\ldots,b_r]$, then $B_s$ is generated over $A$ by $b_1,\ldots,b_r,s^{-1}$. Since $A$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] says $B_s$ is finitely presented over $A$. These neighbourhoods verify exactly local finite presentation as defined by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Combined with the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness from step 5, this is finite presentation of $J\to U$.

Let $h:T'\to T$ be any change of test scheme. The universal Hilbert family pulls back by [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability], and the two projection opens have the universal base-change property of [lem-sfb-graphs-open-in-hilbert]. Under the canonical iterated-fibre-product identifications their projections are $(p_X)_{T'}$ and $(p_Y)_{T'}$. The inverse of $(p_X)_{T'}$ is $(p_X^{-1})_{T'}$, since pulling back $p_Xp_X^{-1}=\mathrm{id}$ and $p_X^{-1}p_X=\mathrm{id}$ verifies both inverse identities. Thus $(p_Y\circ p_X^{-1})_{T'}=(p_Y)_{T'}\circ((p_X)_{T'})^{-1}$, and pulling back $(\mathrm{id},f)$ gives $(\mathrm{id},f_{T'})$ by its two components. The projection identities and the inverse graph bijections therefore pull back exactly, for identities and composites too. For arbitrary $U'\to U$, the same Hilbert theorem supplies $H_R\times_UU'$ and the universal family, and the same open characterization supplies $J\times_UU'$. Equivalently, maps from a $U'$-scheme into this pullback are exactly its $U$-maps into $J$. No argument here requires $T,T'$ or $U'$ to be reduced or Noetherian; the Noetherian hypothesis was used only in steps 1, 5 and 7 over $U$.
